thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher as Street Digests Developments in US-China Trade Talks

title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher as Street Digests Developments in US-China Trade Talks
text:
ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher as Street Digests Developments in US-China Trade Talks December 13, 2018, 09:23:31 AM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Thursday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.4%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.4%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.1%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +0.6%
iShares China Large-Cap ETF ( FXI ): +1.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 0.6%.
US stock futures were on track to open higher as Wall Street continued to focus on developments of trade negotiations between the US and China. China's pledge to increase soybean imports helped offset news of another Canadian being held in Beijing and warnings from the governor of the People's Bank of China that the Chinese economy was slowing.
On Wednesday, China had said it will reduce tariffs on imported autos while US President Donald Trump said he would intervene in the arrest of Meng Wanzhou, the Huawei executive arrested in Canada for violating sanctions on Iran.
Wall Street shrugged off the latest announcement from the European Central Bank that it was holding interest rates unchanged and that it would end its quantitative easing program this month. Although downward revisions to growth and inflation forecasts were viewed as another negative for global economic growth, the central bank said it plans to keep EU interest rates unchanged through the summer of 2019.
In economic data news, the weekly initial jobless claims count totaled 206,000 versus expectations for a decline to 228,000. Continuing claims increased to 1.661 million.
Import prices decreased 1.6% in November after increasing an unrevised 0.5% in October. Excluding oil, import prices decreased 0.3% in November. Export prices decreased 0.9% in November after increasing a revised 0.5% in October. Excluding agriculture, export prices decreased 0.1% in November.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.4% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were inactive.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were also quiet in pre-market trade.
Tailored Brands (TLRD) sank more than 26% after it lowered the outlook for fiscal 2018 adjusted earnings, as Q3 results came in mixed. The company said it was taking a more cautious outlook on Q4 comparable sales for Men's Wearhouse and now expects fiscal 2018 adjusted diluted EPS of $2.30 to $2.35. In October the company guided for $2.35 to $2.50. Analysts are expecting earnings of $2.50 per share, according to Capital IQ. It reported adjusted fiscal Q3 earnings of $1.01 per share, besting the consensus on Capital IQ for $0.94 a share and topping the year earlier GAAP $0.75, with no adjusted items in the comparable quarter. Total company sales were up 0.2% to $812.7 million, missing expectations for $819.5 million. For Q4, the company expects an adjusted diluted loss per share in the range of $0.24 to $0.29. The Street view is a loss of $0.01 per share.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.2% in pre-market trade. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 0.3% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 1.%.
Aflac (AFL) rose more than 4% after it confirmed that it is engaged in discussions with Japan Post Holdings Co. regarding a potential minority investment in the company through open market purchases. The discussions do not involve Aflac or any of its subsidiaries becoming a member of the Japanese group, according to a statement.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rose 0.1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) rose 0.8% after it said it will build a $1 billion campus in Austin, Texas, and establish new sites in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City, California, and expand in several other cities in the next three years. The company said in a statement it's added 6,000 jobs to the US workforce in 2018 and now employs 90,000 people nationwide. The company is on track to create 20,000 jobs by 2023. Austin's new campus will be less than a mile from the company's existing facilities. The expansion will initially accommodate 5,000 additional employees but has the capacity to grow to 15,000, and is expected to make Apple the city's largest private employer.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was quiet and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.2% in pre-market trade.
Total (TOT) ADRs rose more than 1% after it said that it signed a deal to sell a 4% stake in the Ichthys liquefied natural gas project in Australia to its operating partner INPEX for $1.6 billion, reducing Total's project ownership to 26%. According to Total, the divestment is part of its constant portfolio review to optimize capital allocation, though the deal remains subject to Australian regulatory approvals.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.6%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.7%. Natural gas was up 0.9% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 2.9%.
Gold was down 0.3%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.3%. Silver was down 0.4%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 0.1% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were flat in pre-market trade. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was flat.
Marinus Pharmaceuticals (MRNS) fell nearly 9% after it said late Wednesday it priced the sale of 12 million shares of common stock at a public offering price of $3.75 per share. Shares fell by more than 7.5% in the pre-market. The offering size is expected to be $45.0 million, according to a statement. The company has granted to the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1.8 million shares in the offering, which is expected to close on or about Dec. 17.
